questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
One of my main goals for the exchange was to be able to see and explore new things.
First of all, it had to be somewhere I had never been. Another factor was that the weather should either be very cold or very hot compared to Denmark. I choose Brisbane due to the weather, high-tech University, and many options for weekend getaways. QUT had a good amount of subjects I found very interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: QUT uploaded a lot of information for the new International students (almost too much information). Once you get to know their system it's easy to look up information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: QUT offered a lot of different activities in the "welcome week" to get you started. Such as a tour around the campus or around Brisbane. They offered other assistance such as help with housing or choosing subjects.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was very hard. Many struggled with it and ended up with housing offered by QUT. 

I ended up calling the rental agencies and asking to see the rental apartment rather than applying through the online application. We were five people living in a 3 bedroom with a big kitchen/living room area. I shared the room with another girl to be able to afford it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you really want to - it's possible but not always cheaper.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is a first-come, first-served basis. Be aware of the deadlines and the different time zones.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First, you must enroll in more courses than expected, due to some of them might overlap. Once the schedule is online you can choose which subjects and which classes you want to participate.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always write them an email and they were quick to assist you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I missed the release by a few hours and therefore had to rearrange my planned schedule (but it worked out great).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You are able to see the exam form beforehand. Some exams are just written assignments and some are a mix. So you can choose what you like the most.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were more organized and are made on the basis that many come with different professional backgrounds. Therefore I found it easy if I took courses similar to my study.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Your grade is a continuous assessment based on quizzes, presentations, tests in class, and assignments. The final exam then counts the remaining percentages.
You therefore have to always be prepared for every class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Nature's pharmacy, Genes genomes and genetics, Statistics for medical science, Cell's biology,

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Nature's pharmacy was definitely a very good and interesting subject - although the work load was high. 
Genes, genomes, and genetics was a very professional and well-organized course that I would recommend.

questions.answer: Due to renting off campus - the cleaning fee of rental apartments

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee is a lot less expensive and gym membership was more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had organized a few weekend getaways.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I heard a lot about the wave-board club at UQ.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Fraser Island, Binna Burra (national park and place to stay), Scenic rim (National park area) and Burleigh Heads.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy - they were more relaxed and chill.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open-mined and join some social events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The small talks- they are all very friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Try to plan your schedule so you have Friday off to be able to go on weekend trips.
2. Check out Brisbane and its events (Fellons (local beer shop) have free yoga on Wednesday during summer))
3. Check out
flatmates.au
to see if they have any rooms for rent

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pack warm clothes for the first month.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Cliche but all the experiences and new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding the balance and new routine

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun and I envy you guys!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
